title: Unscrew a flashlight's tail cap, pour out its battery and set the flashlight back down
instruction: With your left gripper, grasp the flashlight's body tube from the side, around its middle, and hold it standing head-down on the table. With your right gripper, grasp the tail cap on top from above, about 2 cm down its sides, and unscrew it: turn it counter-clockwise, as seen from above, 400 degrees in total, in two twists of 200 degrees, opening the gripper and turning back between them. The cap rises 1 cm per full turn, so raise the gripper about 5.5 mm during each twist. The cap is free after about one turn: lift it straight up 2 to 3 cm, set it open end down on the table, outside the cardboard box, and let go only once it touches the table. Then lift the flashlight with your left gripper, hold its open end over the box and roll it about 115 degrees until the open end points down, so the battery slides out into the box. Finally roll the flashlight back upright, stand it head-down on the table outside the box, and let go. The cap is 2.6 cm wide and 2.1 cm tall, the body tube 2.2 cm wide, the flashlight 11 cm long.
context: Removing lithium-ion cells is the first step in recycling or servicing small electronics: one hand holds the device while the other unscrews the cover, and the cell is tipped out into a collection box.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Flashlight: a 110 mm 18650 flashlight of black anodised aluminium (34 mm head, 22 mm body tube, 70 g), standing head-down on its bezel at (0.30, -0.02), its 26 mm x 21 mm screw-on tail cap (18 g) up and closed against its collar. The cap's thread is 4-start, 10 mm lead, right-hand: one turn counter-clockwise, seen from above, frees it. Inside: an 18 x 65 mm 18650 lithium-ion cell (47 g, plastic shrink-wrap), its positive end toward the head. Box: an open corrugated-cardboard box (NVIDIA's SimReady open box A06 at one third of its 61.1 x 50.5 x 30.2 cm size) 20.4 cm long (x) and 16.8 cm wide (y), its wall on the robot's left 10.1 cm tall and its wall on the right 4.9 cm, the end walls sloping between them, taped to the table with its centre at (0.50, -0.02), so its near wall is at x = 0.40, in front of the flashlight.
scoring: Five steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video. (1) Body held: a gripper closed on the flashlight body, both fingers touching it, for at least 1 s. (2) Cap off: the tail cap separated from the flashlight (its centre more than 8 cm from the body's centre; assembled it is 4.7 cm). (3) Cap set on the table: a gripper lets go of the cap with the cap's lowest point no more than 2 cm above the table and not over the box, and at the end the cap rests on the table (lowest point within 1 cm of the table top), not over the box, not held. A cap that slips out of the gripper higher up, is dropped, or is knocked onto the table earns nothing for this step. (4) Battery in the box: at the end the battery is out of the flashlight (centre more than 9 cm from the body's) and lies in the box (centre at least 1 cm inside the box's outer walls and less than 6 cm above the table). (5) Flashlight set back on the table: after the battery is in the box, a gripper lets go of the flashlight with its lowest point no more than 2 cm above the table and not over the box, and at the end it rests on the table there (any orientation), not held. Steps 1 and 2 count once reached; steps 3 to 5 are judged at the end, in any order except that step 5 follows step 4. Full score 1.0, ending the run, when all five hold and the three parts have been still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. 0 overall if at the end any part has fallen off the table, or the flashlight body lies in the box (centre over the box's footprint and below its 10.1 cm walls).
reset_notes: Put the battery back in the tube, positive end toward the head, screw the cap on until it seats against the collar, and stand the flashlight on its bezel at its mark, cap up. The box stays taped in place.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The tail cap's 4-start thread, the tube, head and cap collide as signed distance fields, so the cap must be turned about one turn (with 0.2 mm radial clearance) to come off; the battery collides as its convex hull in a bore 0.4 mm wider. The cap's outer shell and the body tube grip like rubber (friction 1.5), standing in for knurled aluminium and compliant finger pads; the threads keep aluminium friction (0.35) and the battery's wrap is slippery (0.1). The springs are visual only, so nothing pushes the battery out. The box is NVIDIA's SimReady open cardboard box scaled to a third, fixed, with signed-distance-field collision. No deformation.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400-step limit; it knocked the flashlight onto its side early and never held it); demo: 1.0 (success at step 953)
